newsitem.title: USA: Anti-takeover measure passes Georgia Senate.
newsitem.headline: Anti-takeover measure passes Georgia Senate.

text.p: The Georgia Senate on Friday approved a measure that could help Healthdyne Technologies Inc fight off a hostile takeover by Invacare Corp.

The measure, which would require publicly traded companies based in Georgia to "stagger" the election of directors, was approved as an amendment to a bill calling for routine revisions in the state business code, legislative officials said.
The measure cleared the chamber by a vote of 52-1.

Officials said the bill now would return to the House, which earlier approved the bill without the amendment. There, the bill will go to a conference committee before landing back on the House floor for a final vote.
The amendment was opposed by Invacare, which has said it intends to propose its own slate of directors for Georgia-based Healthdyne.
Earlier today Invacare said it suspected Healthdyne was behind the measure.
Healthdyne officials were not available for comment.
Healthdyne has rejected Invacare's $13-a-share takeover offer.
